items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: Frisco the drum, they used to call him that too. Oh, Mulefoot, man. Frisco, that's cool. Johnny Frisco. Yeah, yeah, yeah. He used to play with Schillings.

ctx.x: He says he was the leader.

Stein went up and then they sent for Thomas the Barber. That's right. Nah, nah. It wasn't Johnny Stein, it was a Mulefoot. He said Johnny Stein, not the board. Organized to drop this band in New York. That was Rag Baby Stevens. Yeah, yeah. Rag Baby Stevens. Oh, you know, you know what they call that too? Frisco the drum, they used to call him that too. Oh, Mulefoot, man. Frisco, that's cool. Johnny Frisco. Yeah, yeah, yeah. He used to play with Schillings. Yeah, Stein, yeah, that's right.
He used to play with Bromley. Do you remember we played on the boat? On the Capitol? When they had the Battle of Bands, when all the four bands were there.

items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1958-09-24
items.q: In the rhythm section, Johnny Frisco and Eddie Hyman, who's a bass player.

ctx.x: Who did he have in the rhythm section then?
In the rhythm section, Johnny Frisco and Eddie Hyman, who's a bass player. I know him.
Yeah? Eddie? He played with Buck Banville. Yeah, he played with Buck Banville. Buck's my uncle.
